title: An owner's push to a mission source is one recorded command the running integrator applies: no stop, no killed gates, no halt
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, the module comment (the halt rules: "the source's main not where the last landing left it", read only from a fetch that succeeded and only while no other mission's landing on the source is unresolved; "Gates run per mission, on threads"), the mission step (`halt_reason()`, the baseline check and `landing_elsewhere()`, `busy()`), `land()` (the compare-and-swap push, `stale` when main moved, the landing hold), `start_ready()` and how a judging thread records its own outcome; `ensure_mirror()` and `refresh()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/sources.rs; `spawn_source_moved`, `spawn_landing_hold`/`spawn_landing_release`, `spawn_integrator_record` and the `source.moved` case of `spawn_control_apply` in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql; `mission moved` in crates/spawn-cli/src/missions.rs (forward only: `merge-base --is-ancestor`); deploy/ (how the owner deploys today; you may not edit it); docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 and docs/design.md §14 ("所有者的改动同样受它约束" and the assumption between loops: an integrator pass between the owner's push and its `mission moved` halted a mission).

The problem. An owner's push to a mission source costs every running gate. Today it is: stop spawn-integrate, push to the mission's repository, `spawn mission moved --source --from --to`, update the controller, start spawn-integrate. Stopping the integrator kills every running gate of every mission and source: on 2026-11-06 task 48 lost a 40-minute gate that way, and a Supply PA contract push had to wait for mission 4's task 74 gate to finish. Pushing without stopping it lets a pass read the new main before `mission moved` is recorded and halt the mission: "the source's main is X, but the last landing left Y" (a halt only a human resumes). The owner's landing is not a record the integrator can act on; it is an absence of one.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. One owner command. `spawn mission push --source <source> --commit <commit>` (owner login only, like `mission moved`). `<commit>` is resolved in the git repository of the current directory (the owner's checkout; `--repo <dir>` names another), and must be a commit there or already in the source. The command makes it available in the source without touching any branch (it pushes it to `refs/spawn-owner/<full hash>` in the source), then records `source.push_requested` {`source`, `commit`, `ref`, `by`: `human`} and prints `{"request": <that event's id>, "source", "commit"}`. It never moves main itself. With `--wait <seconds>` it also waits for the outcome record (2) and prints it, exiting 0 when applied, 1 when refused, 3 when still pending. The source must be a mission source (`spawn_source_allowed`) with at least one mission; a remote source is refused as `unlandable` is.
2. The integrator applies it, between its own steps, for that source only. On each pass, before the steps of the missions on a source, every pending request for that source (a `source.push_requested` with no outcome record naming it), oldest first, is applied: under the landing hold (`spawn_landing_hold`'s lock, so no task landing's push and its record are ever split by an owner landing), it reads the source's main M; when M is an ancestor of the commit, it moves main from M to the commit with a compare-and-swap (`--force-with-lease`, or `update-ref <new> <old>` in a local source); otherwise it makes a merge commit (first parent M, second parent the commit, by main's merge rules, message naming the owner landing, its request and the commit's subject; author and committer the landing identity) and moves main to it the same way. Then, in the same hold, it records `source.moved` {`source`, `from`: M, `to`: the new main, `missions`: every mission on the source whose baseline was M and is not halted, as `spawn_source_moved` names them, `request`: the request's event id, `by`: `human`}. The fold moves those baselines, as today. A conflict, a commit that is not in the source, or a lease that fails twice records `source.push_refused` {`request`, `reason`} and moves nothing; nothing halts. It does this without the source's mirror (a judging may be using it: work in the source or in a scratch clone), whatever judgings are running on that source or any other, and it never waits for a gate.
3. Never a halt. The owner landing is applied and recorded before any mission step on its source reads main in that pass, so the baseline check never sees a main the owner moved; and a pass that finds a pending request for a source holds every halt by baseline for that source until the request is applied or refused. The halt for a main moved with no record at all (a push behind Spawn's back) stays.
4. Running gates. A gate of another mission or another source keeps running and lands by the usual rules: an owner landing kills, restarts or delays nothing. A gate running on the same source when the owner landing is applied finishes; its verdict is recorded as it comes, and when its landing's compare-and-swap finds main moved, the existing rule in `land()` records `stale` and the task is judged again against the new main (merged and gated again); it is never discarded silently and never counted. The integrator process is never stopped for an owner landing.
5. The old path stays: `spawn mission moved` still records a move the owner made behind Spawn's back. Updating the controller (deploy/) is the owner's step and is out of scope; it no longer needs the integrator stopped.
6. Causality (§14): the owner's landing is a record (the request, then its outcome naming it); the integrator acts on that record, not on a main that changed under it, and nothing depends on which loop ran first.
State the rule in the module comment of integrate.rs (the halt rules, and a new step 0 for owner landings), in docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3, in the usage of `spawn mission`, and in docs/design.md §14 (the owner's pushes). Add unit tests in integrate.rs with a scratch source and mirror, as the landing tests do: a pending request is applied before the baseline check (fast-forward, and a merge when main moved), with one `source.moved` naming it; a conflict is refused and moves nothing; a pending request holds the baseline halt for its source and no other; a judging of the same source whose landing finds main moved records `stale`; and in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/, the records and the fold (`source.push_requested` and `source.push_refused` fold nothing; `source.moved` with `request` moves the named baselines).

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/021.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` (no model judge, no supervisor) runs `alpha` in mission A on source SA and `beta` in mission B on source SB, both gated (accept = gate), on a fake engine; one long-running `spawn integrate` (started once, never restarted) judges through a recording gate that accepts everything and holds a candidate holding alpha.txt or beta2.txt until the scenario releases it. Setup: beta's first task lands on SB, so B has a baseline. The owner works in a clone of SB. It checks:
- (1) while alpha's gate runs on SA, `spawn mission push --source SB --commit <c>` prints a request that is a `source.push_requested` record; within 30 s SB's main is c, a `source.moved` names the request with `from` the old main and `to` c, B's baseline is c, neither mission halts (two more passes too); alpha's gate process is still alive with no record yet, and the integrator is the same process; released, alpha's gate ends `accepted`, once, and alpha lands;
- (2) while beta2's gate runs on SB, a second owner push is applied within 30 s (SB's main is the second commit); released, beta2's records are `accepted stale accepted`: the held gate's verdict, the landing that found main moved, and a second gate whose base is the owner's second commit; beta2 lands on top of it, nothing halts, the integrator is the same process.
On the live main (06cc205; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1): "`spawn mission push --source <SB> --commit <c>` exited 1: spawn: usage: ...". (The same scenario with a plain `git push` instead halts mission B within seconds: "the source's main is X, but the last landing left Y", while alpha's gate runs.) It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
